chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who milked herself from her own milk, and she gave it to her husband so that she would become prohibited to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would keep her, and her back would be struck (with pain).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman breastfeeding her adult husband to become prohibited to him?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the mechanism of 'self-breastfeeding' (Rida' al-Kabir) where a woman breastfeeds her adult husband to establish a mahram relationship, a practice rooted in pre-Islamic customs retained by Shia jurisprudence. The Imam’s ruling to 'keep her' confirms the validity of the marriage, while the detail of 'hurting her back' highlights the physical exertion required, distinguishing it from infant nursing and underscoring its deliberate, albeit arduous, nature. This narration is pivotal in understanding how Shia scholars interpret the flexibility of kinship ties through breastfeeding beyond early childhood.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who milked herself from her own milk, and she quenched her husband in order for her to be Prohibited unto him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would keep her, and her back would be (inflicted with) pain’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and a number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad all from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who drained her milk and made her husband to drink it so that she could become unlawful to him. He (the Imam) said, ‘He keeps her and makes her feel a backache.’” (Such expression is used for a flogging implemented by a judicial body.)
